name: Madagascar
summary: Separated from Africa 160 million years ago, with ninety per cent of its wildlife found nowhere else — lemurs, baobabs, the spiny forest of the south, and rainforest along the eastern escarpment.
when: After the cyclone season, April to November, with whales in July and August.

entries.caption: An Island That Evolved Alone
entries.description: Ninety per cent of what lives here lives nowhere else, because it has been on its own since the dinosaurs.
entries.subject: the avenue of baobabs at Morondava at sunset

entries.caption: Six Ecosystems on One Island
entries.description: Rainforest east, highlands centre, spiny forest south, dry deciduous west, and reef all round.
entries.subject: the tsingy limestone pinnacles of Bemaraha

entries.caption: A Hundred Kinds of Lemur
entries.description: A hundred and seven species and subspecies of lemur, every one of them endemic.
entries.subject: an indri lemur in the rainforest canopy at Andasibe

entries.caption: Not a Safari Island
entries.description: No lions and no elephant — the wildlife here is small, nocturnal, and worth the torchlight.
entries.subject: a chameleon on a branch in Ranomafana rainforest

entries.caption: The Highlands and Maromokotro
entries.description: The central highlands run to two thousand metres; Maromokotro reaches 2,876 in the Tsaratanana.
entries.subject: terraced rice paddies in the Madagascar highlands

entries.caption: The Eastern Escarpment
entries.description: Short, steep rivers off the escarpment, and waterfalls through the rainforest at Andasibe.
entries.subject: a waterfall in rainforest on the eastern escarpment

entries.caption: The Tsiribihina
entries.description: Three days downriver by pirogue through country with no road in it.
entries.subject: a pirogue on the Tsiribihina river at dawn

entries.caption: Nosy Be and the East Coast
entries.description: Reef, whale sharks and humpbacks off Nosy Be, and long empty sand on the east coast.
entries.subject: a white sand beach and turquoise water at Nosy Be

entries.caption: Rainforest and Spiny Forest
entries.description: Andasibe and Ranomafana in the east, and the spiny forest of the south which is like nowhere.
entries.subject: the spiny forest of octopus trees in southern Madagascar

entries.caption: The RN7 and the Tsingy
entries.description: The road south through the highlands, and the limestone tsingy you cross on via ferrata.
entries.subject: a walker crossing the tsingy on a rope bridge

entries.caption: Malagasy, and Eighteen Peoples
entries.description: One language across the island, of Austronesian origin, and eighteen distinct peoples speaking it.
entries.subject: a highland Malagasy village of red brick houses

entries.caption: Famadihana and the Ancestors
entries.description: The ancestors are present here in a way that shapes the calendar and the architecture.
entries.subject: a family tomb standing in highland Madagascar farmland

entries.caption: Romazava and Rice
entries.description: Rice three times a day, and romazava — beef and greens — with it.
entries.subject: romazava and rice served at a Malagasy table

entries.caption: Hira Gasy and Donia
entries.description: Hira gasy troupes in the highlands, and the Donia festival on Nosy Be in June.
entries.subject: a hira gasy troupe performing in the highlands

entries.caption: Silk, Raffia and Zafimaniry
entries.description: Wild silk lambas, raffia work, and the Zafimaniry woodcarving of the south-east.
entries.subject: a woman weaving a silk lamba on a wooden loom

entries.caption: The Rova and the Royal Hills
entries.description: Ambohimanga, the royal hill of the Merina kings above Antananarivo.
entries.subject: the wooden royal compound at Ambohimanga

entries.caption: Pirates and Kingdoms
entries.description: Île Sainte-Marie's pirate cemetery, and the Merina kingdom that unified the island.
entries.subject: the pirate cemetery on Île Sainte-Marie

entries.caption: Antananarivo
entries.description: A capital built up twelve hills, with stairs instead of streets in half of it.
entries.subject: the stepped hillside houses of Antananarivo

entries.caption: Highland Brick
entries.description: Two-storey red brick with a wooden balcony, and nothing else in Africa looks like it.
entries.subject: red brick highland houses with wooden balconies

entries.caption: The Zebu Market
entries.description: Zebu cattle are wealth here, and the markets that trade them are the real calendar.
entries.subject: a zebu cattle market in the Madagascar highlands

entries.caption: Slow, and Worth It
entries.description: Roads are slow and distances are long — but the children will hold a chameleon.
entries.subject: children on a village path in rural Madagascar

entries.caption: Trek, Paddle, Dive
entries.description: Rainforest trekking, the Tsiribihina by pirogue, and reef diving off Nosy Be.
entries.subject: kayaks on the water off a Madagascar reef island

entries.caption: Small Lodges
entries.description: Owner-run lodges at the park gates, and beach places on Nosy Be with a dozen rooms.
entries.subject: a small lodge among trees at a Madagascar park gate

entries.caption: The Reason to Come Carefully
entries.description: Deforestation is the country's crisis, and the parks that work are the ones the villages run.
entries.subject: a reforestation nursery beside a Madagascar rainforest park

entries.caption: Baobabs at Six
entries.description: The avenue at Morondava for twenty minutes at either end of the day, and nothing else like it.
entries.subject: baobabs silhouetted against the sky at Morondava

entries.caption: Masoala
entries.description: The largest protected rainforest in the country, reached by boat, with whales in the bay.
entries.subject: the rainforest of Masoala coming down to the sea

entries.caption: Nowhere Else
entries.description: Lemurs, baobabs, tsingy, spiny forest — none of it exists anywhere else on earth.
entries.subject: a ring-tailed lemur troop in southern Madagascar
